facts.fact: Search costs one action (ACTIONS.search cost 1), spent after the player has picked what to look for and before the Eye roll; a free Search (options.free) costs nothing.

The player picks one of five kinds of thing (healing, comfort, a Murder Weapon, a cleaning tool, a tool) or names one specific thing; the specific request needs a GM online and an empty request is refused before anything is spent.

A room with no Search Tokens left, or a sealed room, refuses the Search with a notice before the action is spent; a roll that reaches the table takes one of the room's Search Tokens (SearchTokens.claim).
What turns up is drawn from the room's table at the tier the total reaches (8, 12, 18 in ACTIONS.search.thresholds; a critical adds one tier); below 8 nothing is found.

A find leaves a Prep Remnant (Faint) only when the thing drawn is a Murder Weapon or a cleaning tool by its category or by a role it carries; a tool that is only a tool, healing and comfort leave none.
The Remnant's visibility is the threshold row's (Hidden at 8, Subtle at 12, Evident at 18) and Obvious on a critical; it is not tied to the crime until the object is used.
The old text differs: it says the room is looted for whatever the player names, while the player mostly picks a kind of thing, and it calls the Remnant a trace.

A Work's total of 12+ adds 1 progress, 18+ adds 2; a critical adds 2 and gives the action back (ACTIONS.project thresholds and critical).
Proposing a new project sends the GM a card with the player's description; no action is spent for it, and nothing exists until a GM approves it.

facts.fact: A project needs a set amount of progress: Trivial 3, Standard 4, Complex 6, Desperate 8 (PROJECT_SCALE).
Each Work costs one action and adds 1 or 2 progress at most (12+ and 18+; a critical 2 and the action back), so a project takes several actions, usually over several times of day.
Only the projects tied to the room the character stands in can be worked on there.
An indirect murder is a project: it adds a Shadow roll to hide the intent when others are in the room, and a roll to hide the Remnants each Work leaves.

facts.fact: Tamper works only on the Remnants in this room that the character has found themselves (the list the GMs build for the Tamper road), or plants a false one (Misleading Trail).
A Tamper costs one action, and only with no action left 1 Sanity instead (PRICE_CHAINS.tamper); the killer cleaning up on their own night pays no action, so for them it starts at the Sanity.

Erasing reads its number off how visible the Remnant is (CLEANUP.dc: Hidden 9, Subtle 12, Evident 15, Obvious 18), lowered by a readied cleaning tool's tier and by 3 while the scene is fresh, before the Investigation; a Reinforced Remnant cannot be erased or reshaped at all.

A reshape is three lower than erasing (CLEANUP.transformAction.dcRelief) and turns the Remnant into a Tamper Remnant with the player's new name and description, which a GM must approve; a critical makes it one band quieter.
Planting a false Remnant points at another character and needs 15 (CLEANUP.actions.misleadingTrail.threshold).

With somebody else in the room, a Shadow roll at 16 to hide what the character is doing comes first (CLEANUP.conceal): a success with Despair costs 1 Sanity, a miss with Hope 1 and with Despair 2, a critical gives 1 back; with no Sanity left to lose and others watching, the Tamper is refused before anything is spent.
The old text differs: "Being watched while you do it is its own problem" stands for the cover roll and its Sanity, and it calls the Remnant a trace.

en.before: You go over a trace you know is here until it is gone or reads as something else, or you leave one that points at somebody else. Being watched while you do it is its own problem.

facts.fact: Sabotage is the third row of the Projects window, not a tile of its own; it costs one action, spent before any roll.
Only a project tied to the room the character stands in can be broken (a Monokuma reaches any room); one already broken and waiting for its repair is withheld.
With other people in the room, a Shadow roll at 16 comes first (SABOTAGE_CONCEAL): a miss means they see roughly what the saboteur is doing; a success with Despair costs -1 on the sabotage roll.
The sabotage roll uses the project's statistic: 12+ makes the project need a simple repair project, 18+ a complex one, a critical one of hidden difficulty; a miss does nothing.
Every attempt leaves a Prep Remnant (Faint): Subtle at 12+, Evident at 18+, Obvious on a critical, Hidden on a miss.
A sabotage roll with Despair, made while others are in the room, tells the room who was seen doing it (DRPG.Action.sabotageSeen).
The old text differs: it says Despair shows the saboteur to the room without the condition that others are there, and it calls the Remnant a trace.

facts.fact: Support costs 1 Hope (HOPE_CALLS.support cost) and grants advantage (grants "advantage") to another character.
The target is picked from the other characters in the caller's room; with nobody else there the Call is refused (DRPG.Calls.nobodyHere).
A Call that grants something to a roll is armed for the next roll of the one it is for: the roll window has the grant switched on and locked, and it is used up by that roll.
A character who already holds an armed Support is refused before the Hope is paid (DRPG.Calls.alreadyArmed).
No Hope Call can be made during an Eclipse, while an Overflow silences Calls, by a dead character, or by one under Silence; the refusal comes before any Hope is paid.

facts.fact: Experience costs 1 Hope and is a needsGm Call.

The experience adds its own value to the roll (Daggerheart's experience modifier); the module adds no number of its own.
No Hope Call can be made during an Eclipse, while an Overflow silences Calls, by a dead character, or by one under Silence; the refusal comes before any Hope is paid.

facts.fact: A plural family on {n}: {n} is the number of projects in this room that can be broken now (sabotageTargetsIn), the hint of the Sabotage row of the Projects window.
The row is greyed out when {n} is 0 (DRPG.Project.nothingToSabotage); the project is picked in a list under the row.
A success makes the project need a repair project (simple at 12+, complex at 18+, hidden difficulty on a critical); it costs one action.
Every attempt, hit or miss, leaves a Prep Remnant.
The old text differs: it calls the Remnant a trace (C5 left the sentence to this batch).

facts.fact: A plural family on {n}: {n} is the number of Remnants in this room that the character has found and that are not Reinforced, the hint of Erase a Trace's row in Tamper's window.
The row is greyed out when {n} is 0, with the reason that only Reinforced ones are left or that the character has found none here.

Erasing reads its number off how visible the Remnant is (CLEANUP.dc: Hidden 9, Subtle 12, Evident 15, Obvious 18), lowered by a readied cleaning tool's tier and by 3 while the scene is fresh, before the Investigation; a Reinforced Remnant cannot be erased or reshaped at all.

A success with Hope or a critical removes it; a success with Despair removes it but leaves an Evident Remnant (Faint); a miss leaves a Subtle (with Hope) or an Evident (with Despair) Remnant and the original stays; a critical also gives back 1 Sanity (CLEANUP.outcome).
The old text differs: it calls the Remnant a trace.

before.one: Wipe out the {n} trace you know about in this room. The easier it is to see, the harder it is to erase.
before.other: Wipe out one of the {n} traces you know about in this room. The easier one is to see, the harder it is to erase.

before.one: Wymaż {n} ślad, o którym wiesz w tym pokoju. Im łatwiej go zobaczyć, tym trudniej usunąć.
before.few: Wymaż jeden z {n} śladów, o których wiesz w tym pokoju. Im łatwiej któryś zobaczyć, tym trudniej go usunąć.
before.many: Wymaż jeden z {n} śladów, o których wiesz w tym pokoju. Im łatwiej któryś zobaczyć, tym trudniej go usunąć.
before.other: Wymaż jeden z {n} śladów, o których wiesz w tym pokoju. Im łatwiej któryś zobaczyć, tym trudniej go usunąć.

facts.fact: The hint of Reshape a Trace's row in Tamper's window; the player then writes a new name and a description for the Remnant.
The number to beat is the erase number less 3 (CLEANUP.transformAction.dcRelief); a Reinforced Remnant cannot be reshaped.
The new name and description go to a GM, who approves or declines the reshape; a declined reshape keeps the roll and the price spent.
A critical also makes the Remnant one band harder to spot (quieter 1) and gives back 1 Sanity (refundStress.critical).
Approved, it becomes a Tamper Remnant (CLEANUP.transformAction.becomes "resolution", labelled Tamper Remnant).
The old text writes the number "three" into the sentence; the code holds it as dcRelief, and no placeholder fills it.

en.before: Rename it and describe it as something innocent. Threshold three lower than erasing; a critical also makes it quieter and hands back the Sanity. It always ends up a Tamper Remnant.

pl.before: Nazwij go inaczej i opisz jako coś niewinnego. Próg o trzy niższy niż przy usuwaniu; krytyk dodatkowo go wycisza i oddaje Sanity. Zawsze kończy jako Tamper Remnant.

facts.fact: The hint of Misleading Trail's row in Tamper's window; {n} is CLEANUP.actions.misleadingTrail.threshold (15), read at the call; the target is another character, picked in a list.
A hit plants a Prep Remnant pointing at the target: Evident with Hope, Subtle with Despair, Obvious on a critical (which also gives back 1 Sanity).
A miss with Hope still plants a Hidden one, Faint; a miss with Despair plants nothing.
The row is greyed out when there is nobody to point at (DRPG.Cleanup.trailNobody).
The old text differs: it calls the planted Remnant a trace.

en.before: Leave something that points at somebody else. Needs {n} or more. A miss with Hope still plants a Faint, Hidden trace; a miss with Despair leaves nothing behind.

pl.before: Zostaw coś, co wskazuje na kogoś innego. Wymaga {n} lub więcej. Chybienie z Hope i tak podkłada ślad Faint i Hidden; chybienie z Despair nie zostawia nic.

facts.fact: The hint of the take row of Palm's window.

On a success the item comes out at random from what the other person carries (Truth Bullets aside); only a critical opens a list to choose from, and backing out of that list still takes one at random.
The Hand roll is against 10 and the Shadow roll against 15 decides whether they notice; noticed, they are told who tried and what was taken.
It costs one action, spent before the two rolls.

en.before: Lift one thing out of their pockets. What comes out is whatever comes out - a critical lets you choose.

pl.before: Wyjmij jedną rzecz z czyjejś kieszeni. Wyjdzie, co wyjdzie - krytyk pozwala wybrać.

facts.fact: A plural family on {n}: {n} is the number of things the character carries that can be left (Truth Bullets aside), the hint of the leave row of Palm's window.
The row is greyed out when {n} is 0 (DRPG.Steal.nothingToPlant); the thing is picked in a list under the row.
Leaving is easier than taking on both rolls: Hand against 8, and Shadow against 13 decides whether they notice (ACTIONS.palm.plant).
It costs one action, spent before the two rolls.

before.one: Put the one thing you are carrying into their pocket.
before.other: Put one of the {n} things you are carrying into their pocket.

before.one: Włóż im do kieszeni tę jedną rzecz, którą nosisz.
before.few: Włóż im do kieszeni jedną z {n} rzeczy, które nosisz.
before.many: Włóż im do kieszeni jedną z {n} rzeczy, które nosisz.
before.other: Włóż im do kieszeni jedną z {n} rzeczy, które nosisz.

facts.fact: A plural family on {n}: {n} is the number of the character's Truth Bullets that can be analyzed now (analysableBullets), the hint of the first row of Analyze's window.
The row is greyed out when {n} is 0, with DRPG.Analyze.noBullets as its reason; the bullet itself is picked in a list below the rows.
A bullet counts while it shows Neutral (or a Key or a Final whose reading is still to buy) and is not locked this chapter by a failed Analyze.
The roll is Head, scored on a GM's browser against the bullet's real kind; a hit shows what the bullet really is, a miss locks it for this player until the chapter ends.

before.one: Work out what your one Truth Bullet not analysed yet really is.
before.other: Work out what one of your {n} Truth Bullets not analysed yet really is.

before.one: Ustal, czym naprawdę jest twój jedyny nieprzeanalizowany Truth Bullet.
before.few: Ustal, czym naprawdę jest jeden z twoich {n} nieprzeanalizowanych Truth Bulletów.
before.many: Ustal, czym naprawdę jest jeden z twoich {n} nieprzeanalizowanych Truth Bulletów.
before.other: Ustal, czym naprawdę jest jeden z twoich {n} nieprzeanalizowanych Truth Bulletów.

facts.fact: The hint of Analyze's Find Stash row; {n} is ACTIONS.analyze.stashThreshold (16) read at the call.

Find Stash is a Head roll scored on a GM's browser: a total of {n} or more, or a critical, finds one concealed stash of another character in this room that this character has not found yet, preferring one with something in it.
Found, the stash is remembered for this character, and the player is told whose it is; below {n}, or with no such stash here, the player reads that nothing was found.
It costs Analyze's price; it needs a GM online, and in a Class Trial the row is not offered and the GMs refuse it, with the price given back.

en.before: Work out whether somebody has hidden something in this room. {n}+ opens one stash to you.

pl.before: Ustal, czy ktoś coś schował w tym pokoju. {n}+ otwiera przed tobą jedną skrytkę.

facts.fact: This is the hint of the first row of Observe's declaration window, "general".
Sweeping the room takes the easiest Remnant on the most relevant shelf: Remnants tied to the crime come first, then by difficulty, and the first one is chosen.
It is settled by the number alone on a GM's browser: no GM reads anything and the player writes nothing.
A room with nothing to find, or a character in no room, sends the roll to a GM's ruling instead.

en.before: Sweep the room for whatever is easiest to spot.

pl.before: Omieć pokój wzrokiem w poszukiwaniu tego, co najłatwiej zauważyć.

facts.fact: This is the hint of the second row of Observe's declaration window, "nonObvious".
Looking past the obvious takes the hardest Remnant on the most relevant shelf (Remnants tied to the crime first), the last one of that shelf.
Only this declaration can also notice a secret project hidden in the room (PROJECT_OBSERVE), against the project's own difficulty; when the room holds no Remnant, that project is the target.
It is settled by the number alone, with no GM reading anything.
The old text differs: "whatever does not belong in this room at all" is not a rule the code runs; what it finds besides the hardest Remnant is a hidden project.

en.before: Look past the obvious: the hardest thing here, and whatever does not belong in this room at all.

pl.before: Spójrz poza oczywiste: na najtrudniejszą rzecz tutaj i na to, czego w tym pokoju w ogóle nie powinno być.

facts.fact: This is the hint of the fourth row of Observe's declaration window, "specific", one of the two rows marked as going to a GM.
The player writes what they are looking for in the window's box before the roll; the roll is thrown first and the request goes to the GMs without the total, so the GM picks blind.
A GM picks which Remnant in the room the request lands on, on a card any GM can open; the total is then scored against that Remnant.
With the box left empty it is scored as a sweep of the room (general), and a notice says so.
No GM listening gives the action back; a request a GM refuses, an empty room or no room sends the roll already thrown to a GM's ruling, never a second roll.

en.before: Say what you are looking for. The GM decides what your gaze lands on.

pl.before: Powiedz, czego szukasz. GM decyduje, na czym zatrzyma się twój wzrok.

facts.fact: The hint of the Dynamic Action tile in the action grid (the sheet builds it, since ACTIONS holds only the tile's place); the tile costs one action.
The player describes what they do in a window (required); the description goes to a GM, who picks the difficulty band and the statistic, or refuses it.
A refused Dynamic Action is told to the player (DRPG.Action.dynamicRefused) and spends nothing; the action is spent only once the GM has set the difficulty, before the roll.

The bands are 8+, 13+, 16+ and 19+ (DYNAMIC_THRESHOLDS: Trivial, Takes practice, Foreign to most people, Demands very niche expertise); a success gets that band's tier, 0 to 3, for a find the GM may hand over.
A success leaves a Prep Remnant (Faint) whose visibility goes the other way from the difficulty: Obvious at the easiest band, Hidden at the hardest; a miss leaves none.
Not found in code as a rule: "gentler thresholds than the universal actions" compares two tables (8/13/16/19 against, for example, Project's 12/18); no function makes that comparison.
The old text says "standard actions"; the glossary's term is universal actions / akcje uniwersalne (DB22, DB34), and "that is the reward for inventing something" is the design's reason (O9).

en.before: Describe what you are doing; the GM sets the difficulty. Dynamic Actions have gentler thresholds than the standard ones - that is the reward for inventing something.

pl.before: Opisz, co robisz; GM ustala trudność. Dynamic Actions mają łagodniejsze progi niż standardowe - to nagroda za wymyślenie czegoś.

facts.fact: The description of the Dynamic Action, shown in its briefing in the description window (dynamicDef).
The player describes what they do in a window (required); the description goes to a GM, who picks the difficulty band and the statistic, or refuses it.
A refused Dynamic Action is told to the player (DRPG.Action.dynamicRefused) and spends nothing; the action is spent only once the GM has set the difficulty, before the roll.

The bands are 8+, 13+, 16+ and 19+ (DYNAMIC_THRESHOLDS: Trivial, Takes practice, Foreign to most people, Demands very niche expertise); a success gets that band's tier, 0 to 3, for a find the GM may hand over.
A success leaves a Prep Remnant (Faint) whose visibility goes the other way from the difficulty: Obvious at the easiest band, Hidden at the hardest; a miss leaves none.
Not found in code as a rule: "gentler thresholds than the universal actions" compares two tables (8/13/16/19 against, for example, Project's 12/18); no function makes that comparison.
The old text says "standard actions"; the glossary's term is universal actions / akcje uniwersalne (DB22, DB34), and "that is the reward for inventing something" is the design's reason (O9).

en.before: Any action at all, provided you describe it in detail - the GM sets the difficulty and the statistic. The thresholds are gentler than the standard actions, as a deliberate reward for inventing something.

pl.before: Dowolna akcja, byle opisana szczegółowo - GM ustala trudność i statystykę. Progi są łagodniejsze niż w akcjach standardowych, celowo, jako nagroda za pomysł.

facts.fact: The note under Despair Flow's assignment table in the GM panel, read by a GM.
Despair from a student's rolls goes to the pool of the Monokuma a GM assigned them to in Despair Flow.
A student nobody assigned falls back to the first pool (the list shows that choice as "{name} (fallback)", DRPG.Assign.fallbackOption).
A student set to "- nobody -" (NO_MONOKUMA) feeds no pool at all; an NPC or a template is the use the code names.
The assignments are the world setting gmAssignments, which every player's browser receives, so a player's browser can read who is set to nobody.
The old Polish says "BN" for NPC (DB32: NPC in Polish too).

en.before: “(fallback)” = never assigned, so the student feeds the first pool. “- nobody -” keeps a student out of every pool - an NPC, a template - and every player's browser can read who is set to it.

pl.before: „(domyślnie)” = nieprzypisany, więc uczeń zasila pierwszą pulę. „- nikt -” trzyma ucznia poza wszystkimi pulami - BN, szablon - a przeglądarka każdego gracza może odczytać, kto jest tak ustawiony.

facts.fact: The hint of the season checklist's row "assignments", read by a GM.
Despair from a student's rolls goes to the pool of the Monokuma a GM assigned them to in Despair Flow.
A student nobody assigned falls back to the first pool (the list shows that choice as "{name} (fallback)", DRPG.Assign.fallbackOption).
A student set to "- nobody -" (NO_MONOKUMA) feeds no pool at all; an NPC or a template is the use the code names.
The assignments are the world setting gmAssignments, which every player's browser receives, so a player's browser can read who is set to nobody.
The row is done when every student is assigned by hand (explicitPool) or set to nobody; the students who fall back to the first pool are named under it until assigned.
The old Polish says "BN" for NPC (DB32).

en.before: Despair from a student's rolls goes to the pool a GM assigned them to in Despair Flow; a student nobody assigned falls back to the first pool and is named here until assigned. A student set to nobody on purpose - an NPC, a template - feeds no pool, and that is fine; every player's browser can read who is.

pl.before: Despair z rzutów ucznia idzie do puli, do której GM przypisał go w Despair Flow; uczeń, którego nikt nie przypisał, trafia do pierwszej puli i jest tu wymieniony, dopóki nie zostanie przypisany. Uczeń celowo ustawiony na nikogo - BN, szablon - nie zasila żadnej puli i tak ma być; przeglądarka każdego gracza może odczytać, kto to jest.
